newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS' SCOTTY BOWMAN EARNS 1,000TH NHL COACHING WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS' SCOTTY BOWMAN EARNS 1,000TH NHL COACHING WIN.

text.p: Detroit Red Wings coach Scotty Bowman Saturday became the first coach in National Hockey League history to record 1,000 regular season career victories.
Bowman reached the unprecedented milestone against one of his former clubs when Brendan Shanahan scored two minutes into overtime to lift the Red Wings to a 6-5 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins.
Bowman coached the Penguins to a Stanley Cup championship in 1991-92.
In a legendary 25-year NHL coaching career with St Louis, Montreal, Buffalo, Pittsburgh and Detroit, the 63-year-old Bowman has compiled an all-time regular season record of 1,000-452-255.
"A long time ago, I said someone was gonna win 1,000 games. That was when I was out of coaching. To win 1,000, you have to be in the right place at the right time," Bowman said.
"Every team I've been with has had great goaltending and a committment to winning."
Bowman had failed in his first two bids to reach the lofty plateau after his Red Wings got him win number 999.

Detroit battled to a 1-1 tie with St Louis Tuesday and lost 7-4 to Vancouver on Thursday. But three turned out to be the charm for both Bowman and Shanahan, who completed a hat trick to give Detroit the victory.
"They're gonna be talking about this win for years," Shanahan said.

"I think as a team, we were all excited to be here. I think to win here in Pittsburgh, where (Bowman) was a coach, was exciting for all of us. I just wanted to make sure I didn't miss the net," added Shanahan.
Bowman also has coached 263 playoff games, giving him a total of 1,162 career wins including post-season play.
He won his first Stanley Cup championship with Montreal in 1972-73 and went on to win three more with the Canadiens and another with the Penguins.
"We had a pretty big championship team," Bowman said of his Penguins roster.
"It's too bad we didn't win another Cup in Pittsburgh," added Bowman, who also guided St Louis and Detroit to the Stanley Cup Finals.
Only Toe Blake, with eight, has won more Stanley Cups as a coach than Bowman.
